title: Friendship (Teresa, Life 8)
hookLine: Teresa says prayer is nothing but friendly intercourse with one who loves us
tomorrow: what if your mind won't sit still long enough to pray?

cards: Some of the best evenings with a friend have no agenda: two people on a porch, the same drink going cold, long stretches with nothing said. Nobody calls that wasted.
Teresa of Avila, a Spanish nun, wrote a book about her own life, and in it she confesses that for a time she stopped praying. Not out of doubt; out of shame. She felt too unworthy to come near God.
Later she calls that a mistake. And her definition of prayer sounds more like the porch than like a speech.

teach.b: Here's her definition, in the sense of chapter eight: mental prayer is nothing other than a close sharing between friends, taking time, often, to be alone with the one we know loves us. Look at what's in it.
And the one who loves us. No method, no posture, no right set of words. Mental prayer here means quiet, inner prayer, not reading words off a page, and what holds it together is the friendship.
That's why shame was the wrong reason to stay away. Even when we don't yet love God the way God loves us, she says, it's worth staying, because this friend bears with our faults.
She leans on something Jesus says in John's Gospel: "Henceforth I call you not servants; for the servant knoweth not what his lord doeth: but I have called you friends."
Here's the line to repeat: servants report in; friends just show up. For Teresa, prayer starts there.
Someone already loves you, and you go to spend time.

how: Carmelite nuns and friars keep set times of silent inner prayer each day, and some other Christians use Teresa's definition of prayer as friendship to begin their own.

games.q: your friend hasn't prayed in months and is too embarrassed to start again: 'God must be tired of me.' what would Teresa tell her?
o: wait until she's fixed herself up first.
come back anyway; this friend bears with our faults.
find a stricter method so it sticks this time.
games.why: Teresa stopped praying out of shame and later called it a mistake: prayer is time with a friend who bears with our faults.

practice: Pour something to drink, tea, coffee, a glass of water, and sit with it the way you'd sit across from an old friend. Smell it, taste it slowly, and let the gaps stay long, with nothing to prove.
If you pray, you can talk to God plainly about today, as across a kitchen table, and leave room just to be there.

wordCard.voice: Friendship. Teresa's picture of prayer: time alone, often, with the one we know loves us.

orig.note: Teresa's Spanish, written in the Latin alphabet: to spend time together as friends do.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: time with a friend, which is how Teresa describes prayer itself. See you soon.
